standard_prerequisites.name: Factoring through a projective module is equivalent to factoring through a free module, and the property is preserved by composition
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: the statement counted by the sibling card S1-algebra-ideal-factor-through-projective at 17711-17735, cited at proof lines 17745-17747
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the factorisation through a free module that the proof then shrinks.

standard_prerequisites.name: A map into a direct sum of copies of the ring has image contained in a finite subsum when the source is finite
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the finite free module through which the map factors.

core_obligations: Use the equivalence between factoring through a projective and through a free module to write the map as a composite whose middle term is a direct sum of copies of the ring (proof lines 17745-17747).
Choose finitely many generators of the source and evaluate the first half of the factorisation on them, noting that each image has only finitely many nonzero coordinates (proof lines 17747-17751).
Conclude that the image is contained in a finite free direct summand, so the map factors through a finite projective module (proof lines 17751-17752).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a factorisation through a free module (proof lines 17745-17747).
Evaluate on finitely many generators and count coordinates (proof lines 17747-17751).
Shrink to a finite free submodule and conclude (proof lines 17751-17753).
difficulty_reason: The lemma upgrades a factorisation through an arbitrary projective module to one through a finite projective module when the source is finite, and the proof is an 8-line argument that inspects the components of the factorisation on generators. It first replaces the projective module by a free one using the equivalence of the two factorisation conditions, then evaluates the first half of the factorisation on finitely many generators of the source, observes that only finitely many coordinates are nonzero for each generator, and concludes that the image lies in a finite free direct summand. The finiteness step is the substance and it is displayed.
